headline: US dollar hits Tk 123 in inter-bank trade
summary: Stronger demand for foreign currency and slower remittance inflows have pushed the exchange rate higher.
details: The US dollar has climbed to Tk 123 in the inter-bank market. This rise is driven by stronger demand for foreign currency and slower inflows of remittances and export earnings.
According to Bangladesh Bank data, the weighted average inter-bank exchange rate stood at Tk 123 yesterday, up slightly from Tk 122.97 a day earlier.
Banks are currently trading the dollar between Tk 122.70 and Tk 123.75. For instance, Prime Bank sold dollars at Tk 123.75 and bought them at Tk 122.75 yesterday.
Bankers attribute the strengthening dollar to mounting payment pressure. Remittance inflows have slowed following the two Eid months, creating a slight shortage of US dollars in the market.
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, CEO of Mutual Trust Bank, noted that the banking sector is facing payment pressure from government imports, particularly fuel and fertilisers, which has pushed the rate higher.
In June, Bangladeshi expatriates sent home $2.81 billion in remittances, down from $2.82 billion in the same month last year. This figure was 18.17 percent lower than the previous month.
The central bank has stopped buying US dollars from the market since June 8 to manage the increased demand. Between July 2025 and June 2026, the BB bought $6.4 billion to build reserves.
As of July 9, gross foreign exchange reserves stood at $31.90 billion under the BPM6 calculation method, up from $24.44 billion a year earlier.
The rate increase comes as an International Monetary Fund (IMF) fact-finding mission is visiting Bangladesh to assess a proposed loan package worth nearly $4.5 billion.
